Online and mailed registrations must be received by Oct 26, 2026 (8 days before Election Day). In-person registration at the county auditor's office is available through Election Day, Nov 3. Ballots must be postmarked by Nov 3; ballots deposited in an official drop box must be in by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

offices: Governor; U.S. House (all districts); Statewide offices & Legislature
notes: Same-day voter registration is available at the polls on Election Day. Mail registrations must be postmarked by Oct 14, 2026, and online registration closes that day at 11:59 p.m. Registration at the municipal clerk's office or other designated location closes Oct 30 at 5 p.m. or at close of business, whichever is later. In-person absentee voting may begin Oct 20; municipalities set their own schedules, and in-person absentee applications end no later than Nov 1. Requests for absentee ballots by mail (including online, email or fax) are due by 5 p.m. on Oct 29, 2026. Absentee ballots must be delivered to the polling place or central-count location by 8 p.m. on Nov 3.

offices: U.S. Senate; U.S. House (all districts); State Legislature
notes: State legislative seats also on the ballot; no Governor race in 2026 (next in 2028). Absentee applications are due Oct 28, 2026. Absentee ballots hand-delivered to the clerk's office are due by Nov 2, 2026. Mailed ballots postmarked by Nov 3 are accepted if received by the canvass-convening hour on Nov 9, 2026; mailed ballots without a postmark are accepted if received by the day after the election (Nov 4, 2026). Electronic ballot return (for eligible military, overseas, and physically disabled voters) must be received by close of polls on Nov 3.

offices: U.S. Senate; Governor; U.S. House (all districts); Statewide offices & Legislature
notes: Same-day voter registration available (register and vote at the polls on Election Day). Advance registration closes Oct 19, 2026. Absentee ballots may be requested at any time before the day of the election; the last day to request one is Nov 2, 2026. In-person absentee voting runs Oct 6 through Nov 2, excluding county holidays.

offices: U.S. Senate; Governor; U.S. House (all districts); Statewide offices & Legislature
notes: Held only for Nov 3 races in which no candidate receives the required majority (Georgia requires a majority to win the general election). Registration deadlines: Oct 5, 2026 for state and local runoff races; Nov 2, 2026 for federal runoff races. Absentee ballot applications are due by Nov 20, 2026.

offices: Judicial & special-election runoffs
notes: Listed on the official calendar as 'General/Special Runoff Election Day'; held only for races (e.g., nonpartisan judicial contests or special elections) in which no candidate wins the required majority on November 3.

offices: U.S. House (districts without a majority winner); Other open-primary offices without a majority winner; State Senate District 14 special primary (East Baton Rouge Parish)
notes: Officially the 'Open U.S. Representative General/Open General/Special Primary (State Senator, 14th Senatorial District, Parish of East Baton Rouge) Election.' The general-election round is held only for races in which no candidate wins the required majority on Nov 3 (U.S. House districts without a majority winner, plus open-primary judicial/local races); the same day also holds a special primary for State Senate District 14 in East Baton Rouge Parish. Online (GeauxVote) registration deadline is Nov 21; early voting runs 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m., excluding Sunday, Nov 29. Absentee ballot requests are due by 4:30 p.m. Dec 8, and a registrar must receive a voted absentee ballot by 4:30 p.m. Dec 11 (military, overseas and hospitalized voters follow separate rules). Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
